As someone that just got into Table Top gaming... I have to say that Dominion is the best tabletop game I've played. Again, I haven't played that many so take it for what you will but I like it so much because everyone starts out the same and whoever has the superior strategy will win.

It's a deck building game, but you build your own deck from cards that are available on the table to every other player. The game starts you out with a few coin cards and a few victory points. The point of the game is to build your deck enough to be able to afford and buy victory cards. Whoever has the most points at the end of the game is the winner. The thing is, the actual victory cards are absolutely worthless while in play, so you don't want to over saturate your deck with them. You have to balance buying action cards, money and victory points.

The strategy you adopt will vary game to game, because you only play with 10 Kingdom cards; these are the cards that allow you to do different things, whether it's giving your opponents curse cards that will subtract a point from their score or having them reveal their next hand to you and you decide if they keep it or pass on it. The base game comes with about 25 Kingdom cards but you only play with 10 at a time. Meaning that you have a LOT of combinations of cards and they all have their own synergy. I've played countless games with friends and I haven't had a game that felt the same.

Thing is though, if he's already into tabletop gaming, he probably has this game. However, there are a bunch of expansions for it (and one more just recently came out in the past couple months) so if you're all out of ideas and he likes this game, get him an expansion he doesn't have.

Ascension! I've heard that it's very similar to Dominion, which a couple other folks have suggested so far. 2-4(6 with at least 2 sets) players all start with the same 10 card deck, and take turns using the cards in their hand to get either runes to acquire Heroes and Constructs with, or power to defeat Monsters with. Heroes are played, have an effect, and get discarded at the end of the turn. Constructs stay in play, and generally have smaller effects, but they last throughout the game. Monsters will give points, and usually have some other effect(Draw two cards, each opponent discards a construct, etc). The goal is to have the most points at the end of the game. There is a point pool that starts with 60-120 points, depending on how many people are playing. As you get points, they come out of the point pool. When the pool runs out, you finish the round, and add up how many points you got throughout the game, as well as the point value from all the cards in your deck(Example: The 2 in the star). Gameplay is pretty fast(I've had a few 10 minute games on the app), depending on the expansion, how many people are playing, and how well they know the game. There isn't a huge amount in the way of screwing over other players, it tends to mostly be competing for the same resources, but that varies depending on expansion.
